items.title: A bounded degree Borel graph on a Ramsey space has an independent tail
items.author: Balazs Bursics; Zoltan Vidnyanszky
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 540-542: for a bounded degree Borel graph on the Ramsey space and a pair of finite and infinite data satisfying the standard ordering condition, there is an infinite subset of the given tail on which the induced graph has no edges. The proof (source lines 543-550) is short but does two things the statement does not show: it defines an auxiliary graph on the interval by declaring two elements adjacent when some of their restrictions are adjacent in the original graph, and it checks that this auxiliary graph is irreflexive with degree bounded by two to the n times the original degree; only then does the classical colouring theorem apply and a colour class give the independent tail. The statement records only the existence of the independent set.

proof_spans.label: the complete author proof of the labelled lemma, retained line for line
